issues.t: Lower intake manifold gasket leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant level keeps dropping with no obvious puddle, a sweet smell, a rough idle or misfire, the temperature gauge creeping up, or oil that looks milky or like chocolate milk on the dipstick.
issues.why: The original plastic-framed gaskets under the intake manifold on the 3800 V6 break down over time, partly from old Dex-Cool coolant. Coolant then seeps into the engine valley or straight into the oil, where it destroys the bearings if left alone.
issues.next: If coolant keeps disappearing, have a shop pressure-test the cooling system and check the oil for coolant. Replace the gaskets with the updated metal-framed type and change the oil and coolant at the same time. Do not keep driving if the oil looks milky.

issues.t: Plastic upper intake manifold cracks and leaks coolant
issues.sym: Coolant leaking or crusting near the throttle body at the top of the engine, coolant loss with no outside leak, white exhaust smoke, or overheating.
issues.why: The upper intake (plenum) is made of plastic. Coolant runs through it, and the hot EGR passage next to it slowly eats away the plastic until it cracks or the coolant passage leaks, sometimes into the engine.
issues.next: Get unexplained coolant loss checked soon. Coolant pulled into the cylinders can bend engine parts. The fix is GM's revised upper intake and gasket kit, often done together with the lower intake gaskets.

issues.t: Backfire when starting can break the upper intake manifold (recall)
issues.sym: A loud pop from under the hood while cranking the engine, followed by the engine running badly or not at all. The plastic upper intake can split.
issues.why: A backfire during startup can crack the plastic upper intake manifold. GM recalled these cars to reprogram the engine computer to reduce the chance of a backfire.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer to confirm the recall reprogramming was done. If the intake has already cracked, it must be replaced before the car will run properly.

issues.t: Leaking fuel pressure regulator can cause a backfire and fire (recall)
issues.sym: Fuel smell, a long crank before starting, black smoke, or a loud backfire while trying to start the engine.
issues.why: Certain fuel pressure regulators on the 3800 V6 leak through their internal diaphragm. Fuel is drawn into the intake through the vacuum hose, and a backfire on a failed start can split the intake, knock a fuel injector loose and start a fire.
issues.next: Check your VIN on NHTSA.gov for recall 04V-090. If the car smells of fuel or backfires, do not keep cranking it. Have it towed to a dealer or shop.

issues.t: Power window falls into the door or stops working
issues.sym: A window drops down inside the door, goes up crooked, makes a grinding or snapping noise, or the motor hums but the glass does not move.
issues.why: The window regulator uses a cable on plastic pulleys and guides. The plastic cracks and the cable comes off its drum or snaps. This is the most-reported LeSabre complaint, especially for 2000 to 2002.
issues.next: Tape or prop the glass up to keep rain out until it is repaired. Usually only the regulator needs replacing, and the motor can often be reused.

issues.t: Automatic transmission slips or loses gears
issues.sym: Engine revs flare between shifts, the car feels like it is in neutral for a moment, a gear is missing, or the transmission goes into a limp mode and stays in one gear.
issues.why: The 4-speed automatic wears internally with age and mileage. GM bulletins describe burnt fourth-gear clutches, slipping and shift shudder, as well as valve body problems that cause loss of drive.
issues.next: Check the fluid level and color first. Burnt-smelling or dark fluid is a bad sign. Have the codes read and get a transmission diagnosis before it fails fully, since driving on a slipping transmission makes the damage worse.

issues.t: Harsh or erratic shifting from a failing pressure control solenoid
issues.sym: Hard, banging shifts or soft and slipping shifts, often with a check engine light and codes like P1811 or P0748.
issues.why: The electronic pressure control solenoid inside the transmission sets how firmly each gear engages. When it wears out, line pressure becomes wrong and shifts become harsh or slip.
issues.next: Have the codes read. If the solenoid is at fault it can be replaced through the transmission side cover without removing the transmission, which is far less work than a rebuild.

issues.t: Fuel gauge reads wrong or sticks
issues.sym: The fuel gauge reads full or empty no matter how much gas is in the tank, jumps around, or the low-fuel light comes on too early or too late.
issues.why: The fuel level sensor on the pump assembly inside the tank wears out. Its contact strip wears through and sends a wrong signal to the gauge. This is the LeSabre problem reported most often to RepairPal.
issues.next: Track your fill-ups by the trip odometer so you do not run out of fuel. The fix is a new sender, which usually means replacing the fuel pump module.

issues.t: Front wheel bearing hums and sets the ABS light
issues.sym: A humming or growling noise that rises with speed and changes when turning, sometimes with the ABS and traction control lights coming on.
issues.why: The front wheel bearing and hub is a sealed unit that wears out. Its built-in wheel speed sensor can also fail, which turns on the ABS warning.
issues.next: Have the bearings checked for play and noise. Replace a bad hub soon, since a badly worn bearing can overheat or let the wheel wobble.

issues.t: Harsh clunk into reverse or drive when cold
issues.sym: A hard bang or jolt when shifting into reverse or drive on cold mornings, which goes away once the car warms up.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins for cold-weather harsh engagement on this transmission, usually traced to valve body or control issues.
issues.next: Mention the symptom to a shop and ask about GM's bulletins. If shifting becomes harsh when warm too, or slipping starts, get a full transmission check.

issues.t: Rusted floor under the rear-seat battery
issues.sym: Corrosion or holes in the floor pan around the battery under the rear seat, a damp or musty smell, or battery acid stains.
issues.why: The battery on these LeSabres sits under the rear seat. Acid fumes and moisture can corrode the floor pan around it, and GM issued a bulletin about this corrosion.
issues.next: When replacing the battery, look under the rear seat cushion for rust and make sure the battery vent tube is attached. Treat or repair any rust early.

issues.t: Misfire from corroded fuel injector connections
issues.sym: A flashing or steady check engine light, rough running, and misfire codes, often on one cylinder.
issues.why: GM found that the fuel injectors can suffer fretting corrosion where they connect, causing a cylinder to misfire.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A shop can test the injector and its connector, then clean, reseal or replace the faulty injector.

issues.t: Oil leak from the oil pan or rear main seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, oil on the bottom of the engine or where the engine meets the transmission, and a burning-oil smell.
issues.why: GM issued bulletins for repeat oil pan gasket leaks and released a new rear main seal for the 3800 V6.
issues.next: Keep an eye on the oil level. A shop can clean the area and find the exact leak before replacing a gasket.

issues.t: Shake or vibration at highway speed
issues.sym: The steering wheel or seat shakes at highway speeds on smooth roads.
issues.why: GM issued a long series of bulletins for highway shake on these cars, usually traced to tire and wheel balance or out-of-round tires.
issues.next: Have the tires and wheels balanced and checked for out-of-round. A road-force balance usually fixes it.

issues.t: Inner tie rod nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Wandering, loose or uneven steering, or a knock from the front end.
issues.why: On some 2000 LeSabres the inner tie rod nuts could work loose, and a tie rod could separate, causing an unexpected steering input.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 99V-301. Have the steering checked right away if it feels loose.

issues.t: Loose brake booster nuts can affect braking (recall)
issues.sym: A low brake pedal, a pedal that feels loose, or brakes that do not fully release.
issues.why: The nuts holding the brake booster to the pedal assembly could be loose or missing on some cars. If they come off, braking can be lost.
issues.next: If the brake pedal sinks, feels soft or goes closer to the floor, or a red brake warning comes on, slow down gently, use a lower gear, and pull over where it's safe. Don't drive on: call for a tow. Check your VIN for recall 99V-238. Do not drive the car if the brake pedal feels loose or sinks.

issues.t: ABS unit can leak internally (recall)
issues.sym: ABS or traction control warning lights, or brakes that act strangely in hard stops.
issues.why: Some 2000 LeSabres had internal fluid leaks in the ABS hydraulic unit, which could affect rear brake balance, ABS, traction control or stability control.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 00V-114. The dealer inspects the ABS unit and replaces it if needed.

issues.t: Headlight aim adjuster does not work (recall)
issues.sym: Headlights that seem aimed too far left or right and cannot be adjusted with the built-in horizontal adjuster.
issues.why: The horizontal headlamp adjuster on some cars did not move the reflector, so the lights could not be aimed correctly that way.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 99V-355. Have the headlights aimed by a shop using the optical method GM added to the owner's manual.

issues.t: Driver airbag inflator can fracture (recall)
issues.sym: There may be no warning before a crash. The airbag light may or may not be on.
issues.why: On some cars the driver airbag inflator could break at a weld when it deployed, sending pieces into the cabin and leaving the bag underinflated.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-222. The dealer inspects the driver airbag module and replaces it if needed, free of charge.

issues.t: Steering gear bolts missing or loose (recall)
issues.sym: Uneven steering response or clunking noises when turning.
issues.why: Some cars were built with steering gear mounting bolts that were missing or not tightened properly.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 02V-067. The dealer checks both bolts and tightens or replaces them.

issues.t: Chimes, interior lights or power locks act up (recall)
issues.sym: The key-in-ignition or seat belt chimes do not sound, interior lights do not work right, or the power door locks misbehave.
issues.why: A damaged capacitor in the module that controls alarms, lights and locks could disable these functions.
issues.next: Ask a Buick dealer whether the module recall was done. The dealer inspects the module and replaces it if needed.

issues.t: Rust on the rocker panels
issues.sym: Bubbling paint or rust along the rocker panels below the doors.
issues.why: GM issued a service alert about rocker panel corrosion on these LeSabres.
issues.next: Wash salt off the underside in winter and treat surface rust early. Have deep rust checked by a body shop.
